candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — disinfection, sterilization, and reprocessing
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — sterilization versus disinfection
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate the microbial endpoints of sterilization and disinfection.

options.A: Sterilization and disinfection have the same microbial endpoint
options.B: Sterilization is limited to environmental surfaces and is not used for instruments
options.C: Sterilization destroys fewer microorganisms than high-level disinfection
options.D: Sterilization is intended to eliminate all forms of microbial life, whereas disinfection does not reliably eliminate all bacterial spores

candidate.rationale: CDC defines sterilization as a process that destroys or eliminates all forms of microbial life. Disinfection eliminates many or all pathogenic microorganisms on inanimate objects but, unlike sterilization, does not reliably eliminate bacterial spores. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Sterilization destroys/eliminates all forms of microbial life; disinfection eliminates many or all pathogenic microorganisms but not bacterial spores reliably.
